family.title: Family emergency planning | Court Forms Online
family.description: Find free child caregiving forms and family preparedness plans for ICE detention, deportation, hospitalization, and other temporary separations.
family.heading: Plan for your family in an emergency
family.intro: Prepare documents about who can care for your child if you are detained by ICE, deported, hospitalized, or otherwise unavailable. Find free, step-by-step tools for the states listed below.
family.resourceIntro: Don’t see your state or the form you need? These nonprofit legal organizations offer additional forms, PDF packets, and planning guides for families facing detention or deportation.
family.resourceAdvice: Choose forms for the state where your child lives and follow the signing instructions. A form from another state may not work for your family. {legalHelp} if you need help choosing a form.
family.clinicDescription: The Catholic Legal Immigration Network’s directory covers all 50 states and Washington, D.C. Find links to guardianship and power of attorney resources, legal help, and consulates.
family.appleseedTitle: Appleseed: Child safety plans by state
family.appleseedDescription: Download English and Spanish PDF guides with sample legal forms for selected states. The Appleseed Network also links to other organizations’ state-specific family planning packets.
family.appleseedLink: Find Appleseed’s state guides and forms
family.ilrcDescription: The Immigrant Legal Resource Center offers a fillable, printable toolkit with emergency contacts, children’s information sheets, and a document checklist. Its caregiver authorization affidavit is for California only.
family.maDescription: Massachusetts forms from the Massachusetts Law Reform Institute and legal services partners include caregiver authorization, temporary agent appointment, and child information sheets. PDF packets are available in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Haitian Creole, and Arabic.
family.maLink: Get Massachusetts forms and PDF packets
family.faqIntro: Plan ahead for who will care for your children and make school, medical, and other decisions if you cannot be there.
family.detentionQuestion: How can I plan for my children if I am detained by ICE or deported?
family.detentionFirst: If you are at risk of immigration detention or deportation, choose a trusted adult who agrees to care for your children. Talk about both a short separation and a longer absence: where the children would live, how to stay in contact, and who could make school and medical decisions. A family preparedness plan puts these arrangements and important contacts in writing.
family.detentionSecond: Use {appleseed} to explore care arrangements and sample forms. If a parent is already detained or deported, {urgentHelp} about the child’s care and any urgent court steps.
family.absenceQuestion: Can these forms help during surgery, a hospital stay, or another temporary absence?
family.absenceFirst: You may need someone else to care for your child while you recover from surgery, receive treatment for a serious illness, or are away for work or travel. Depending on your state and situation, a caregiver authorization or temporary agent appointment may let that person make decisions while you are unavailable.
family.absenceSecond: Check which situations the form covers and when it starts and ends. Different forms may apply to immigration emergencies and other absences. For example, Massachusetts Legal Help explains {temporaryAgent} separately from its immigration emergency packet.
family.temporaryAgent: appointing a temporary agent for work, sickness, or travel
family.typesQuestion: What is the difference between a caregiver authorization, a power of attorney, a temporary agent appointment, and guardianship?
family.typesCaregiver: A caregiver authorization may let another adult make certain school or health care decisions. In California, for example, the form is called the {caregiverForm}.
family.typesPowers: A power of attorney may authorize another person to make certain decisions for a child. Massachusetts also has a form called a temporary agent appointment. The names, decisions you can delegate, and time limits vary by state and form.
family.typesGuardianship: In a guardianship, a court appoints a guardian. Depending on the state and type of guardianship, the appointment may affect who makes decisions for the child and how the guardianship can end.
family.typesAdvice: The right choice depends on state law, existing custody orders, and the other parent’s rights. Read each form’s instructions and {legalHelp} if you are unsure which arrangement fits your family.
family.careQuestion: What information should I leave with my child’s caregiver?
family.careFirst: Write down emergency contacts, school and doctor information, medications, allergies, health insurance, and your child’s daily needs. Gather important documents such as birth certificates, relevant custody orders, and signed caregiving forms. Keep them in a safe place your chosen caregiver can access, and explain how to reach you and your lawyer if you have one.
family.careSecond: The {packets} include checklists and child information sheets to help you organize these details.
family.dependentQuestion: Can I also plan for bills, property, or other family members who depend on me?
family.dependentAnswer: Yes. Detention, deportation, or a medical emergency may also interrupt rent payments, access to money, or care for an adult dependent. You may need separate arrangements or legal documents for those needs. {clinic} links to state resources about guardianship, powers of attorney, and financial planning, as well as legal help.
family.missingStateQuestion: Where can I find forms if my state is not listed?
family.missingStateAnswer: Our {guided} cover the states listed in the form finder. For other states or additional documents, use the {packets} from nonprofit legal organizations above. Choose a resource for your state. A caregiver or guardianship form from another state may have different requirements.
